figures.caption: Figure 1. Workflow of CSP with MTP and active learning. The process begins with the generation of initial structures, including amorphous and random structures, corresponding to a target composition AxByCz. The CSP loop iteratively updates the MTP model by fitting to newly selected query structures derived from active learning, ensuring accuracy between DFT and MTP predictions. The predicted structures are validated through energy comparisons and radial distribution function (RDF) analysis against reference structures to assess prediction accuracy.

figures.caption: Figure 2. (a) Energy difference (ΔE) between most stable predicted and experimental structures calculated using PBE and SCAN functionals. Blue circles represent results obtained from PBE functional, and green triangles represent those obtained from SCAN. Red crosses indicate cases where PBE failed to identify the correct ground-state structure. (b) Classification of 12 experimentally known structures based on prediction outcomes. Blue and red regions indicate cases where the predicted structure is more stable than the experimental reference and cases where the predicted and experimental structures match, respectively. The overlapping region represents structures for which both the predicted and reference phases were successfully identified.

figures.caption: Figure 3. (a) Classification of predicted crystal structures based on polyhedral connectivity: corner-sharing (left, blue), edge-sharing (middle, orange), and mixed corner/edge-sharing (right, green). Li-ion diffusivity (D600 K), obtained from AIMD simulations over 60 ps at 600 K, and relative potential energy (Erel) of predicted 10 most stable structures for (b) Li2SiS3, (c) Li2GeS3, (d) Li4SiGeS6, and (e) Li4SiSnS6. The shape and color of scatter points indicate the polyhedral connectivity types: corner-sharing (blue circles), edge-sharing (orange circles), and mixed corner/ edge-sharing (green triangles). The purple bars represent Erel with respect to the most stable predicted structures. The x-axis represents the relative stability ranking, ordered from most stable to least stable. The insects depict representative crystal structures with their corresponding polyhedral connectivity.

figures.caption: Figure 4. Isosurface of Li-ion probability density distribution and self-part of van Hove correlation function for different polyhedral topologies in Li2SiS3 and Li4SiGeS6: (a) corner-sharing and (b) edge-sharing topologies. (c) Enlarged view of Li-ion pathways in edge-sharing topologies. (d) Schematic illustration of dead volume formation in corner-sharing topologies. (e) Comparison of center-to-center distances between adjacent polyhedra in corner- (dc) and edge-sharing (de) topologies. (f) Distribution of polyhedron volume in corner- and edge-sharing topologies. figures.caption: Figure 5. Analysis of 10 most stable predicted structures for (a) Li2SiS3 and (b) Li4SiGeS6 compositions in terms of the packing ratio (green bars), average Li−S4 polyhedron volume (height of circles), and CSM (circle color). Data are extracted from AIMD simulations at 600 K over 60 ps. The packing ratio (α) quantifies the nonconductive volume fraction, while CSM reflects the degree of distortion in the Li−S4 polyhedron. The shape of the base markers represents polyhedral connectivity: blue circles (corner-sharing), orange squares (edge-sharing), and green triangles (corner/edge-sharing).
